teaser.text: Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. helps people and organizations arrange insurance, manage risk and administer claims. Its central economic role is that of an intermediary: a dollar comes in for arranging or servicing risk, while the insurer—not Gallagher—usually pays covered losses.

stock.title: Gallagher stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Gallagher stock forecast with bear, base and bull scenarios, the cash-generation test, and the valuation measures behind the share-price outlook.
stock.opening: The weighted scenario is $117.56 in October 2027 and $136.92 in October 2029. It hinges on retention, integration and cash conversion.
stock.closing: The full memo also covers Gallagher’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Gallagher’s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to substantial downside from today’s $254.88. The weighted price is $117.56 in October 2027 and $128.83 in October 2028. It reaches $136.92 in October 2029, equivalent to losses of 53% and 47% with dividends included at the first two dates. The final loss is 43%.

The 2029 range is wide: $87.76 in the bear case to $214.85 in the bull case. The bear probability is 30% and the base probability is 55%. The bull probability is 15%, making the base path the central outcome despite its projected 40% loss by 2029.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Gallagher?

paragraphs.text: The bear case uses revenue of $16,300 million, $17,000 million and $17,700 million, with margins of 8.3%, 8.5% and 8.7%. The bull case uses $17,500 million, $19,000 million and $20,700 million, with margins of 10.2%, 10.8% and 11.3%. The bear reflects weaker new business, producer departures and delayed integration; the bull reflects retention, faster synergies and better cash conversion. Historical net income has been uneven, while the AssuredPartners synergy target remains a future run rate. The earnings specialist assigns 25% to bear, 55% to base and 20% to bull.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Gallagher really make?

paragraphs.text: Cash conversion asks how much reported profit becomes cash from operations. Gallagher’s “real free cash flow” starts with operating cash, subtracts capital spending and then subtracts stock-based pay. In 2025, free cash flow was $1,785 million and real free cash flow was $1,736 million. Real free cash flow represented 12.5% of revenue in 2025, compared with 20.8% in 2024.

dividend.title: Gallagher dividend
dividend.meta_description: Gallagher’s dividend history, cash-flow coverage, outlook and current yield, with the price context behind them.
dividend.opening: Gallagher’s forecast shows dividends per share rising from $2.95 to $3.15 and then $3.35. Gallagher generated $1,785 million of free cash flow and $1,736 million of real free cash flow in 2025, with cash mainly directed to acquisitions and dividends.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines Gallagher’s business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Gallagher pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises from $2.95 per share to $3.15 and then $3.35. The bear holds at $2.80 before a small increase to $2.86, reflecting pressure from debt and integration spending. The bull reaches $3.62 by 2029, requiring an approximately $0.91 quarterly rate. The base remains below the roughly 7.9% historical dividend growth rate because acquisitions compete for cash.

blocks.heading: Does Gallagher’s dividend come from its cash flow?

paragraphs.text: Cash conversion asks how much reported profit becomes cash from operations. Gallagher’s “real free cash flow” starts with operating cash, subtracts capital spending and then subtracts stock-based pay. In 2025, free cash flow was $1,785 million and real free cash flow was $1,736 million. Real free cash flow represented 12.5% of revenue in 2025, compared with 20.8% in 2024.
For most of the past five years, Gallagher’s cash went mainly toward acquisitions and dividends, while new equity and debt made the AssuredPartners purchase possible.

paragraphs.text: Management guides to 2026 organic growth of 6% across Brokerage and Risk Management. The split is 5% in Brokerage and 9% in Risk Management. It guides to adjusted Brokerage EBITDAC margin of 35.1%–36.3%, with underlying improvement of 40–60 basis points. AssuredPartners is expected to produce $3,025 million of revenue and $1,057 million of adjusted EBITDAC. Annualized synergies target $160 million by year-end 2026, rising to $325 million by early 2028.
